methods: writing cos as sin of complement
statement: Find all solutions in the interval $0\\le x<2\\pi$ of the equation $\\sin3x=\\cos2x$.
solution: Since $\\cos2x=\\sin(\\pi/2-2x)$, the equation becomes $\\sin3x=\\sin(\\pi/2-2x)$. Hence either $3x=\\pi/2-2x+2\\pi k$, giving $5x=\\pi/2+2\\pi k$ so $x=\\pi/10+2\\pi k/5$; or $3x=\\pi-(\\pi/2-2x)+2\\pi k=\\pi/2+2x+2\\pi k$, giving $x=\\pi/2+2\\pi k$. In $[0,2\\pi)$ the first family yields $x=\\pi/10,\\pi/2,9\\pi/10,13\\pi/10,17\\pi/10$ and the second yields $x=\\pi/2$ (already listed). Thus the distinct solutions are $\\pi/10,\\pi/2,9\\pi/10,13\\pi/10,17\\pi/10$.
